newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Cricket-Zimbabwe score historic win over India.
newsitem.headline: Cricket-Zimbabwe score historic win over India.

text.p: The dramatic improvement in Zimbabwe cricket which began against England two months ago continued with a brilliant three wicket defeat of India in the day/night match at Centurion Park on Friday.

Zimbabwe bowled out India for 216 in 48.4 overs and, after rain had reduced their target to 171 from 34 overs, they got home at 171 for seven with two balls to spare. It was the first time Zimbabwe had beaten India in 14 attempts.

The heroes for the part-timers were all rounders Craig Evans (43 from 47 balls with three sixes) and Paul Strang (31 not out from 42 balls). They put on 71 for the seventh wicket after Zimbabwe had seemed to be down and virtually out at 78 for six.
When Evans was caught on the boundary Strang and Heath Streak got the target down to nine runs from the last over, bowled by Venkatesh Prasad.
Streak scrambled four runs from the first two balls and then heaved a full toss over midwicket for the boundary which tied the scores, before scampering the winning single off the next delivery.
When India batted they struggled to break the shackles of a superbly disciplined bowling and fielding effort from Zimbabwe.
Sachin Tendulkar (41) and Mohammad Azharuddin (44) put on 70 for the fourth wicket, but only Ajay Jadeja's quickfire 36 threatened to raise the run rate towards the end of the innings.

Rain fell at the start of the supper break and play eventually resumed at 2050 local time with a revised target. Zimbabwe reached 46 for one in the ninth over, but then collapsed, losing five wickets for 32 runs in 10 overs.
The two sides meet again in the final pool match at Benoni on Sunday. Zimbabwe are now favourites to meet South Africa in next Wednesday's final due to a superior run rate.
Bowling: Brandes 9.4-0-44-2 (w4), Rennie 8-1-26-1 (w1), Streak 10-2-42-1 (w2), Whittall 5-0-20-1 (w2), Strang 9-0-43-1, Evans 2-0-13-0, Campbell 2-0-8-1, G.Flower 3-0-14-0
Bowling: Srinath 7-0-32-0 (nb2 w3), Prasad 6.4-0-39-1 (nb2 w2), Kumble 7-0-31-1, Ankola 5-0-32-1 (w2), Singh 7-1-18-2 (nb1), Tendulkar 1-0-11-0
